commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Mochi and implement Level-0 greeting
Implement Level-1 echo: echo commands and exit on bye
Implement Level-2 add/list: store tasks and display them on request
Implement mark command to mark tasks as done
Implement unmark command to reverse done status
Add Task class and refactor Mochi to use it (A-Classes)
Support todo, deadline, and event task types
Add Todo, Deadline, Event subclasses of Task (A-Inheritance)
Add test-ui skill and UI test plan for regression testing
Handle unknown commands and empty todo descriptions
Handle all invalid commands via MochiException (A-Exceptions)
Add error-handling test cases to UI test plan
Implement delete command to remove tasks
Store tasks in an ArrayList instead of a fixed-size array (A-Collections)
Add delete test cases to UI test plan
Introduce a TaskType enum to represent task types (A-Enums)
commitResults.messageBody:
The task type is the natural candidate for an enum: each subclass
currently hardcodes its own display symbol ('T', 'D', 'E') as a string
literal. Add a TaskType enum (TODO, DEADLINE, EVENT) carrying that
symbol, store the type on the Task base class, and have the subclasses
pass it up instead of repeating the literal. This removes the duplicated
tag constants and gives the type a first-class identity that the upcoming
save/load increment (Level-7) will also need.

Command verbs were considered as an alternative enum but rejected: the
short, tested if-else chain in Mochi.handleCommand would only gain a
mapping layer, whereas the task type is domain data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save and load tasks from disk automatically (Level-7)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add file-based persistence so tasks survive across sessions. On startup,
Mochi loads any previously saved tasks from data/tasks.txt; after every
add, mark, unmark, or delete it writes the current list back out.

Design:
- Storage: handles file I/O. Creates data directory and an empty file
  if either does not exist at startup (handles the first-run case).
  Corrupted lines are silently skipped.
- TaskList: wraps List of Task; every mutating operation (add, remove,
  mark, unmark) calls Storage.saveTasks to keep the file in sync.
- Task.toFileString and Task.fromFileString: serialise/deserialise using
  the pipe-delimited format with the TaskType tag letter.
- Mochi: loads via Storage on startup, delegates mutations to TaskList.

Also:
- Updated test-ui runner to clean the data directory between test cases
  so saved tasks do not leak across tests.
- Added data/ to .gitignore.

Store deadline and event dates as java.time.LocalDate instead of plain
strings. Accept yyyy-mm-dd (ISO) format on input and display dates as
MMM d yyyy (e.g., Oct 15 2019) using Locale.ENGLISH.

Changes:
- Deadline and Event now hold LocalDate fields; constructors accept
  LocalDate directly.
- Mochi parses /by, /from, /to arguments with LocalDate.parse and
  throws MochiException on non-ISO dates.
- Task.fromFileString reads ISO dates from the data file; corrupted
  dates are rejected as corrupted data.
- Tests updated to use ISO dates; added test 10 (date formatting) and
  test 11 (invalid date format error).

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-8' into master (Level-8: Dates and Times)
Refactor into OOP design with Command pattern (A-MoreOOP + A-Packages)
commitResults.messageBody:
Extract closely related code into well-defined classes following good
OOP principles:

Classes:
- Ui: all user interaction (welcome, goodbye, errors, task display)
- Parser: static parse() converts raw user input to Command objects
- Command hierarchy: abstract Command with execute() and isExit()
  - ExitCommand, ListCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand
  - AddTodoCommand, AddDeadlineCommand, AddEventCommand
- Storage: now accepts a configurable file path
- TaskList: unchanged (already well-factored)
- Mochi: main class with constructor + run() loop

Packages:
- mochi: Mochi, Parser, Storage, TaskList, MochiException
- mochi.command: Command and all concrete commands
- mochi.task: Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskType
- mochi.ui: Ui

The main loop now reads:
  Command c = Parser.parse(fullCommand);
  c.execute(tasks, ui);
  isExit = c.isExit();

This replaces the 80-line if-else chain with polymorphic dispatch.
Each command class owns its own validation and execution logic.

Change mainClass from seedu.duke.Duke to mochi.Mochi and the shadow JAR
file name from duke.jar to mochi.jar to match the actual project.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for Parser and Task (A-JUnit)
commitResults.messageBody:
ParserTest (15 tests): verifies that Parser.parse() returns the correct
Command type for each verb, and throws MochiException with the expected
message for invalid inputs (unknown verb, missing task number, missing
/by /from /to, etc.).

TaskTest (16 tests): verifies Task.fromFileString() round-trips through
toFileString() for all three task types (Todo, Deadline, Event) in both
done and not-done states. Also tests error handling for corrupted data:
too few parts, invalid done flag, unknown type, missing date fields,
and unparseable dates. Tests markAsDone/markAsNotDone status flipping.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Javadoc comments to all public classes and methods (A-JavaDoc)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add descriptive Javadoc to public constructors and methods across all
packages: Mochi, TaskList, Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskType,
MochiException, and all Command subclasses. Override methods inherit
parent Javadoc via {@inheritDoc}.

Stretch goal: header comments now cover all non-private classes,
constructors, and methods.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add SE-EDU Java and Git coding standard skills (A-CodingStandard)
commitResults.messageBody:
Create project-specific skills to enforce SE-EDU conventions:

- seedu-java-coding-standard: intermediate-level Java coding rules
  (naming, layout, statements, comments) from se-education.org
- seedu-git-standard: commit message and branch naming conventions

Update AGENTS.md to mandate these standards for all code and commits.
The existing codebase already conforms to the SE-EDU Java standard.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command for keyword search (Level-9)
commitResults.messageBody:
Implement 'find <keyword>' that searches task descriptions for the
given keyword and displays matching tasks. The search is case-sensitive
and matches against the full toString() representation of each task.

New files:
- FindCommand: streams task list and filters by keyword containment
- Parser: 'find' verb with empty-arg validation
- Ui.showMatchingTasks(): displays matching tasks with numbering

Test cases 12-13 added to verify find with results and no results.

Add the checkstyle Gradle plugin with the SE-EDU intermediate coding
standard rules. Fix all violations in the main and test source files:

- Reindent switch-case blocks so that case labels and bodies line up
  with the configured caseIndent.
- Move the unused mochi.TaskList import out of Ui.
- Remove unused test imports (assertTrue, LocalDate).
- Rewrap assertThrows lambdas so '(' is not the first character on a
  line, per the SeparatorWrap rule.
- Split long error-message strings across multiple lines.

No user-visible behaviour changes.

Add a JavaFX GUI to Mochi, following the SE-EDU JavaFX tutorial. The
application now launches via the mochi.gui.Launcher entry point, which
opens a window built from MainWindow.fxml and DialogBox.fxml in
src/main/resources/view/, with avatar images in src/main/resources/images/.

- Ui now writes to a configurable PrintStream so its output can be
  captured, letting the GUI build replies without touching the console.
- Mochi gains a no-arg constructor (JavaFX needs one) and a getResponse
  method that returns the reply text for a single user input.
- MainWindow and DialogBox controllers form the GUI, and the welcome
  message is shown on startup.
- build.gradle adds the JavaFX dependencies (17.0.7 for win/mac/linux)
  and points the application main class at mochi.gui.Launcher.
- The text UI is unchanged and still covered by the test-ui suite; the
  test script now excludes the JavaFX gui package when compiling, since
  its bare javac invocation lacks the JavaFX libraries.
- Add MochiTest to verify getResponse; document the GUI in the UI test plan.

Convert TaskList.add to accept a variable number of tasks via Java
varargs (Task... tasks), and use it in Mochi's constructor to bulk-load
the tasks saved to disk in one call. The varargs method also removes the
need for an explicit loop when several tasks are added at once.

- TaskList.add(Task) becomes TaskList.add(Task...).
- Mochi now calls tasks.add(storage.loadTasks().toArray(new Task[0])).
- Add TaskListTest covering the varargs overload.

No user-visible behaviour changes.

Use the Java assert feature to document assumptions that must hold at
various points in the code, per the A-Assertions increment:

* TaskList treats callers as responsible for validating indices before
  remove/mark/unmark; the assertion catches out-of-bounds calls.
* TaskList never accepts a null task when adding.
* Task always has a non-null type and description after construction.
* Storage guarantees the parent data directory exists before writing.

Java assertions are disabled by default, so they add no overhead in
normal runs; they serve as executable documentation that surfaces bugs
during testing when run with -ea.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplicated code in UI and command loop
commitResults.messageBody:
showTaskList and showMatchingTasks both print a numbered task list
under a divider; extract the common shape into showNumberedList.

run and getResponse both parse, execute, and catch command errors;
extract that shared behaviour into executeCommand so each entry
point only worries about where its input comes from and where its
output goes.

mark, unmark, and delete all repeat the same bounds check and error
message before touching the task list. Let's move that check into
TaskList.requireValidIndex so the list owns its own index policy and
keyword commands need only one line to validate, keeping execute at
a single level of abstraction.

commitResults.messageTitle: Trim duplication when adding and loading tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Add commands re-fetched the freshly added task from the list by
index; let's reuse the task object they already created, which makes
the intent obvious and avoids the (size - 1) lookup.

Task.fromFileString repeated the same if (isDone) markAsDone() block
for every task type; extract applyDoneFlag so the restore path is
easier to read.

mark/unmark/delete all typed parseTaskNumber(args) - 1, a conversion
whose meaning is not obvious. Let's introduce toZeroBasedIndex so
call sites read as the conversion they actually perform.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use streams when processing task lists
commitResults.messageBody:
Use the Streams API where a list is built from another collection,
per the A-Streams increment:

* Storage maps each task to its file line and joins them, so the
  whole file is written in one pass.
* TaskList exposes findByKeyword built with filter + toList, and
  FindCommand delegates to it instead of rebuilding the query.
* Ui prints a numbered list with IntStream.range, expressing the
  index loop declaratively.

Behaviour is unchanged; output strings are identical.
A-Assertions: Document assumptions with Java assertions
A-CodeQuality: Refactor for code quality

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/mochi/ui/Ui.java
A-Streams: Use streams when processing task lists

Add the D-Notes extension, which lets the user record short snippets
of text for future reference (e.g., their waist size or a movie title
to remember).

New commands:
* note <text> - add a note
* notes - list all notes
* delete-note <index> - remove a note by number
* find-note <keyword> - search notes by keyword

Notes are persisted to a notes.txt file stored next to the task file,
independent of the tasks file. The note commands mirror the patterns
established by the existing task commands.

Storage is refactored into shared loadLines/writeLines helpers so the
task and note persistence paths keep a single implementation.

The note commands are covered by a new UI test case (Test 14) and the
existing suite still passes.
D-Notes: Support managing notes

Add the D-Places extension, which lets the user record details about
places they want to remember, such as restaurants and study cafes.

New commands:
* place <name> /d <detail> - add a place with one detail
* places - list all places
* view-place <index> - show the details of a place
* delete-place <index> - remove a place
* find-place <keyword> - search places by name or detail

Places are persisted to a places.txt file stored next to the task
file, using the same pipe-delimited format as tasks. Command.execute
now receives a PlaceList alongside the task and note lists, so every
command can dispatch on all three data stores.

Covered by a new UI test case (Test 15); the existing suite still
passes.
D-Places: Support recording place details

Harden the command parser so that common user mistakes are handled with
clear, verb-specific feedback instead of surprising behaviour.

Key changes:
* Leading/trailing whitespace in the raw command is now trimmed; an
  empty command produces a dedicated message.
* Description fields are normalised by collapsing runs of whitespace
  into a single space, so accidental double spaces are tolerated.
* Index arguments (mark, unmark, delete, delete-note, delete-place,
  view-place) now produce an error message that names the right kind
  of list and an example that uses the correct verb.
* A blank or whitespace-only todo description is now caught in the
  parser rather than in AddTodoCommand, consistent with how the other
  add commands behave.
* Event ordering is validated: the end date must not be earlier than
  the start date.
* Duplicate parameters (/by, /from, /to, /d) are detected early with
  a dedicated error message.
* Adding a place whose name already exists is now rejected.

No user-visible phrase changes are made in this increment; the
existing suite continues to pass.
A-MoreErrorHandling: Harden input parsing and error messages

Add comprehensive JUnit 5 tests to cover nearly all code that can be
tested automatically, raising coverage significantly above the starting
34 tests.

New test classes:
* TodoTest, DeadlineTest, EventTest – direct construction, display
  format, and toFileString for each task type.
* PlaceTest – name/detail storage, contains matching, file round-trip,
  and corruption handling.
* NoteListTest, PlaceListTest – add, remove, keyword search, index
  validation, and automatic file persistence.
* StorageTest – round-trip persistence for tasks, notes, and places;
  graceful handling of missing files and corrupted data lines.

Expanded existing test classes:
* ParserTest – all new note/place commands, blank/whitespace input,
  duplicate-parameter detection, verb-specific index error messages.
* TaskListTest – mark/unmark display, remove return value, index
  validation, and keyword search.
* MochiTest – end-to-end note/place lifecycles, duplicate place
  rejection, event date ordering, whitespace normalisation.

The existing text-UI suite (15 cases) continues to pass unchanged.
A-MoreTesting: Add comprehensive JUnit 5 tests
